explainers.title: Input Interactions Standard
explainers.function: apps/web inputs: before/after of rule I1-I11
explainers.html:
Edit where it is shown, count, choose

AIA's input standard (I1–I11), shown on four screens from develop @ 44b66ef. Today AIA opens a full-screen modal holding one text box 11 times. The standard removes every one of them. Light and dark use the product's tokens.

  • I1 · Edit in placeClick the value, type. Enter saves, Esc restores, the save state shows beside it.
  • I2 · CountBounded numbers get a stepper with the bounds stated. A value out of range is refused, never clamped.
  • I3 · ChooseA known set gets chips, a segmented control or a combobox. If the system knows the list, nobody types it.
  • I5 · Create in the list"+ New" becomes a row where the thing will live. Enter creates it and opens the next row.
  • I6 · UndoA reversible delete happens at once, with "Vrátit" for 8 s.
  • I7 · Modals are rareOnly for money, ledger decisions and irreversible actions. Never for a single text field.

1. Creating a folder in a client's knowledge

KnowledgeArea.tsx:319: "Nová složka" opens AskDialog, a showModal() dialog over a dimmed page. Renaming a folder or a label does the same. Two lines above it, "Nový štítek" is already an inline form.

3. A question's options

Where a modal stays

Starting a run whose cost reaches the study's limit, lifting a budget, approving a report, activating a methodology version, approving a Deep Research policy, a Lead change that reaches every client, archiving a client. Each one interrupts because it spends money or records a decision that cannot be taken back. The modal states the consequence and the cost, and focuses the safe choice.

The full inventory (~250 entry points), the fix list and the plan are in .planning/evidence/input-interactions-audit.md and .planning/plans/input-interactions.md. The plan is proposed for the scope baseline. Prototype references: prototypes/research-lead-v2/src/components/ui.tsx:52 (Item) and :108 (AddItem).

questions.title: May a search query ever carry Class A material?
questions.context: Your Q20 note: 'maybe even class A, depends how the query is constructed'. Class A is the client's own material: their uploaded sources, their approved knowledge, their notes. Today nothing Class A leaves AIA except to the approved EU model route. A query built from it would send the client's own words to a search provider outside the EU.
questions.example: A client's internal report says their new product is code-named 'Projekt Lípa' and launches in Brno in March. Under (a), the Lead may search only from the design and public context ('nápoje bez cukru Brno 2026'), and never 'Projekt Lípa'. Under (b), code builds the query from approved fields of the client's knowledge (category, market, competitors), never free text. Under (c), the Lead may quote the report in a query.

options.label: Never Class A
options.detail: Queries are built from the design (Class B) and public context only

options.label: Only fields code extracts
options.detail: Category, market, named competitors from approved knowledge; never the client's free text or documents

options.label: Class A allowed
options.detail: Any client material may shape a query

questions.rationale: It gives the specific, reputable searches you want ('competitor X, Czech market') without sending a client's confidential text to a provider outside the EU. Code, not the model, picks the fields.

questions.title: Search operators ("Google search hacking") in the MVP?
questions.context: Your Q20 note: build advanced search operators into the workflows to find highly specific, reputable sources. Brave's API supports operators like site:, filetype: and intitle:. Today queries are plain text written by the investigators. Adding operators touches Deep Research's query planning, which is frozen except for defects, so it needs your yes as a scope change.
questions.example: A Design Research track on Czech dairy consumption sends 'site:czso.cz filetype:pdf spotřeba mléka 2025' and 'site:mze.gov.cz "mléčné výrobky" zpráva'. That finds the ČSÚ and ministry reports directly instead of blogs. A curated list of reputable domains per topic (ČSÚ, Eurostat, ministries, academic repositories) is kept in Settings.

options.label: In the MVP, from a curated domain list
options.detail: Code composes operators from a reviewed list of reputable domains and file types per topic; the model proposes, code validates

options.label: In the MVP, model-written operators
options.detail: The model writes operators freely; RetrievalGate still checks every URL

questions.rationale: It's what makes the sources reputable rather than just specific, and a curated list keeps code in charge of where queries go. It's a small change around the frozen engine rather than inside it.
